nodes.label: @Failover placement rules (CGLIB proxy)
nodes.rationale: The annotation only works where the AOP proxy can intercept: public, non-static, non-final method on a non-final concrete bean, called from another bean. Interface beans (Feign, Spring Data, @HttpExchange) are the exception since Spring uses a JDK interface proxy there. A startup WARN flags un-advisable concrete-class placements; self-invocation is a runtime call-graph property and cannot be detected statically.

nodes.label: Expression-based expiry (expiryDurationExpression / expiryUnitExpression)
nodes.rationale: Expressions resolve from properties, environment variables or any Spring EL, and take priority over the fixed attributes, so expiry can differ per profile/environment without recompiling.

nodes.label: Domain grouping on @Failover
nodes.rationale: All annotations in one domain must agree on expiry — a mismatch makes the last writer overwrite the stored expiry timestamp, so a startup WARN is logged when detected.

nodes.label: @Failover attribute resolution order
nodes.rationale: Non-blank expression attributes override their fixed counterparts; expiryPolicy overrides the default policy but expiryDuration/expiryUnit still supply defaults when the policy delegates; keyGenerator overrides the default generator; payloadSplitter enables scatter/gather mode.
